headline: Croatia's Clinical Strike Sinks Panama in Toronto
story: Panama came to Toronto bristling defensively—a five-four-one formation that invited Croatia to break them down. And break them down they did, controlling 52 per cent possession with a relentless high press. The visitors' superior ball recovery (13.2 seconds to Panama's 16.9) told the tale: they were sharper, more organised, more likely to transition possession into threat. The turning point came in the 54th minute, when a clinical finish burst Panama's resistance and set the template for an increasingly comfortable evening.

Croatia's 0.94 expected goals betokened not dominance but sloppiness in the final third. They took their most clear-cut chance—a 0.80 xG shot in the 54th—and converted ruthlessly. Then came the panic: successive opportunities of 0.51 and 0.48 xG arrived at 57 minutes (one saved, one missed). Panama, suffocated by a disciplined five-four-one, never got close enough: their 0.69 xG came from eight shots, only one on target. The Croats' recovery time advantage proved decisive in a match that should have been more comfortable than the scoreline suggested.

keyMoment.text: Fifty-fourth minute: Croatia's ruthless 0.80 xG conversion punctures Panama's defensive shape and shifts momentum irreversibly.

home.verdict: Defensive discipline could not mask attacking impotence.
points: Eight shots, one on target: conversion rate (0.69 xG) reveals wide finishing and poor shot selection.
Recovery time lag (16.9s vs Croatia's 13.2s) meant perpetual defensive reset and lost transition moments.
Big chances squandered: 0.20 and 0.15 xG misses at 60 and 68 minutes cost them any realistic path back.

away.verdict: Clinical in the moment; profligate soon after; survived sloppy finishing.
points: Converted 0.80 xG chance in 54th: one clear-cut opportunity decided it against a defensive setup.
Wasted 0.51 and 0.48 xG at 57 minutes; against elite opposition, such profligacy would have proven catastrophic.
Ball recovery dominance (13.2s vs 16.9s) and high-press intensity (4.9 phases vs 3.6) controlled tempo without threat.

statLine: One 0.80 xG chance: all Croatia needed to beat Panama, whose eight shots (one on target) mustered just 0.69 expected goals.
